chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: The challenge of the new music and the Los Angeles scene
summary: He liked bebop as a challenge, with sessions competing with Lucky Thompson, and the scene picked up when Dizzy and Bird arrived.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What appealed to you, though, about the new music specifically? It allowed you to do different things?

Yeah. Well, the reason why I liked it was because it was a challenge. Like, can you do this and can you do that? With most of the guys that was playing, they could do this and they could do that. Like, Lucky Thompson was out there at the time, you know. And every session we'd get on, we'd always see who did what. Which was like a challenge to make you aware of what you was doing.
Well, it was a pretty active scene out there, Central Avenue and Hollywood...
Yeah. When Dizzy came out there with Bird, it really did pick up, because Bird was something...an institution within himself. I mean, pshew.
